title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes a snapshot of 749 customers to identify churn drivers. The overall churn rate is 37.7%. Key findings indicate that Monthly contracts and an identifiable at-risk segment are the primary drivers of customer loss. Lifetime value is significantly higher for Premium subscribers, and recent signup cohorts show slightly elevated churn rates compared to previous years.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and an average monthly fee of $42.11.
Churn rates vary slightly by plan. The Basic plan has the highest churn rate at 38.9%, followed by Standard at 36.7% and Premium at 36.6%.
Analyzing signup cohorts, the 2024 cohort has the highest churn rate at 39.8%, while the 2022 cohort has the lowest at 36.7%.
Contract type is a major churn driver. Monthly contracts exhibit a 48.3% churn rate, which is a 121.1% increase compared to the 21.9% churn rate for Annual contracts.
A specific at-risk segment was identified: 100 customers with high support tickets (>=5) and low satisfaction (<=2). This group has a critical churn rate of 71.0%.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0) with a standard deviation of 13.2 months. The average satisfaction score is 3.42, though 27 customers have missing satisfaction data.
Lifetime value (LTV) correlates strongly with plan tier. Premium LTV is $1,816.78, which is 292.0% higher than the Basic LTV of $463.46.

limitations: The dataset is a single snapshot and does not reflect real-time churn dynamics.
Satisfaction scores are missing for 27 customers (3.6% of the total), which may bias the satisfaction analysis.
The analysis assumes the 'lifetime_value' field accurately represents customer value; the calculation method for this metric was not verified in this stage.
conclusion: To reduce churn, the business should prioritize converting Monthly customers to Annual contracts and focus retention efforts on the identified at-risk segment with high support tickets and low satisfaction. The significantly higher LTV of Premium customers justifies investment in upselling strategies.
